definitions.ADAPT: To make suitable; to make to correspond; to fit or suit.
definitions.APPLE: A common, round fruit produced by the tree Malus domestica, cultivated in temperate climates.
definitions.BLAZE: A fire, especially a fast-burning fire producing a lot of flames and light.
definitions.BONUS: Something extra that is good; an added benefit.
definitions.BRAIN: The control center of the central nervous system of an animal located in the skull which is responsible for perception, cognition, attention, memory, emotion, and action.
definitions.BREAD: A foodstuff made by baking dough made from cereals.
definitions.CHAIR: An item of furniture used to sit on or in, comprising a seat, legs, back, and sometimes arm rests, for use by one person. Compare stool, couch, sofa, settee, loveseat and bench.
definitions.CHARM: An object, act or words believed to have magic power (usually carries a positive connotation).
definitions.CHEST: A box, now usually a large strong box with a secure convex lid.
definitions.CLOCK: An instrument used to measure or keep track of time; a non-portable timepiece.
definitions.CORAL: A hard substance made of the limestone skeletons of marine polyps.
definitions.CREST: The summit of a hill or mountain ridge.
definitions.CRISP: A thin slice of fried potato eaten as a snack.
definitions.DANCE: A sequence of rhythmic steps or movements usually performed to music, for pleasure or as a form of social interaction.
definitions.DELTA: The fourth letter of the modern Greek alphabet Δ, δ.
definitions.DRIFT: (physical) Movement; that which moves or is moved.
definitions.EAGLE: Any of several large carnivorous and carrion-eating birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked bill and keen vision.
definitions.EARTH: The third planet of the Solar System; the world upon which humans live.
definitions.ELITE: A special group or social class of people which have a superior intellectual, social or economic status as, the elite of society.
definitions.FIELD: A land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; open country.
definitions.FLAME: The visible part of fire; a stream of burning vapour or gas, emitting light and heat.
definitions.FLINT: A hard, fine-grained quartz that fractures conchoidally and generates sparks when struck.
definitions.FROST: A cover of minute ice crystals on objects that are exposed to the air. Frost is formed by the same process as dew, except that the temperature of the frosted object is below freezing.
definitions.GHOST: The spirit; the soul of man.
definitions.GRAIN: The harvested seeds of various grass food crops eg: wheat, corn, barley.
definitions.GUEST: A recipient of hospitality, specifically someone staying by invitation at the house of another.
definitions.HAPPY: A happy event, thing, person, etc.
definitions.HEART: A muscular organ that pumps blood through the body, traditionally thought to be the seat of emotion.
definitions.HONEY: A viscous, sweet fluid produced from plant nectar by bees. Often used to sweeten tea or to spread on baked goods.
definitions.HORSE: Any of several animals related to Equus ferus caballus.
definitions.HOUSE: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.
definitions.HUMOR: The quality of being amusing, comical, funny.
definitions.IMAGE: An optical or other representation of a real object; a graphic; a picture.
definitions.IVORY: The hard white form of dentin which forms the tusks of elephants, walruses and other animals.
definitions.JUMBO: An especially large or powerful person, animal, or thing.
definitions.KARMA: The sum total of a person's actions, which determine the person's next incarnation in samsara, the cycle of death and rebirth.
definitions.KIOSK: A small enclosed structure, often freestanding, open on one side or with a window, used as a booth to sell newspapers, cigarettes, etc.
definitions.KNACK: A readiness in performance; aptness at doing something.
definitions.LATCH: To close or lock as if with a latch.
definitions.LAYER: A single thickness of some material covering a surface.
definitions.LIGHT: Visible electromagnetic radiation. The human eye can typically detect radiation (light) in the wavelength range of about 400 to 750 nanometers. Nearby shorter and longer wavelength ranges, although not visible, are commonly called ultraviolet and infrared light.
definitions.LUNAR: The middle bone of the proximal series of the carpus in the wrist, which is shaped like a half-moon.
definitions.MAGIC: The application of rituals or actions, especially those based on occult knowledge, to subdue or manipulate natural or supernatural beings and forces in order to have some benefit from them.
definitions.MANGO: A tropical Asian fruit tree, Mangifera indica.
definitions.MUSIC: A series of sounds organized in time, employing melody, harmony, tempo etc. usually to convey a mood.
definitions.NIGHT: The period between sunset and sunrise, when a location faces far away from the sun, thus when the sky is dark.
definitions.NOVEL: Newly made, formed or evolved; having no precedent; of recent origin; new.
definitions.OCEAN: One of the large bodies of water separating the continents.
definitions.OLIVE: A tree, Olea europaea, cultivated since ancient times in the Mediterranean for its fruit and the oil obtained from it.
definitions.OPERA: A theatrical work, combining drama, music, song and sometimes dance.
definitions.OZONE: An allotrope of oxygen (symbol O₃) having three atoms in the molecule instead of the usual two; it is a blue gas, generated from oxygen by electrical discharge.
definitions.PAINT: A substance that is applied as a liquid or paste, and dries into a solid coating that protects or adds color/colour to an object or surface to which it has been applied.
definitions.PANEL: A (usually) rectangular section of a surface, or of a covering or of a wall, fence etc.
definitions.PEACE: A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony; absence of violence. For instance, a state free from civil disturbance.
definitions.PIXEL: One of the tiny dots that make up the representation of an image in a computer's memory.
definitions.PIZZA: A baked Italian dish of a thinly rolled bread dough crust typically topped before baking with tomato sauce, cheese and other ingredients such as meat, vegetables or fruit.
definitions.PLANT: An organism that is not an animal, especially an organism capable of photosynthesis. Typically a small or herbaceous organism of this kind, rather than a tree.
definitions.POWER: Ability to do or undergo something.
definitions.PULSE: A normally regular beat felt when arteries are depressed, caused by the pumping action of the heart.
definitions.QUART: A unit of liquid capacity equal to two pints; one-fourth (quarter) of a gallon. Equivalent to 1.136 liters in the UK and 0.946 liter (liquid quart) or 1.101 liters (dry quart) in the U.S.
definitions.QUEEN: A female monarch. Example: Queen Victoria.
definitions.QUICK: Raw or sensitive flesh, especially that underneath finger and toe nails.
definitions.RAVEN: Any of several, generally large and lustrous black species of birds in the genus Corvus, especially the common raven, Corvus corax.
definitions.RIVER: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
definitions.SCOUT: A person sent out to gain and bring in tidings; especially, one employed in war to gain information about the enemy and ground.
definitions.SHARE: A portion of something, especially a portion given or allotted to someone.
definitions.SHARP: The symbol ♯, placed after the name of a note in the key signature or before a note on the staff to indicate that the note is to be played a semitone higher.
definitions.SLEEP: To rest in a state of reduced consciousness.
definitions.SNAKE: A legless reptile of the sub-order Serpentes with a long, thin body and a fork-shaped tongue.
definitions.SOLAR: Of or pertaining to the sun; proceeding from the sun.
definitions.SOUTH: One of the four major compass points, specifically 180°, directed toward the South Pole, and conventionally downwards on a map, abbreviated as S.
definitions.SPORT: Any activity that uses physical exertion or skills competitively under a set of rules that is not based on aesthetics.
definitions.STAFF: (plural staffs or staves) A long, straight, thick wooden rod or stick, especially one used to assist in walking.
definitions.STEEL: An artificial metal produced from iron, harder and more elastic than elemental iron; used figuratively as a symbol of hardness.
definitions.STONE: A hard earthen substance that can form large rocks.
definitions.STORM: Any disturbed state of the atmosphere, especially as affecting the earth's surface, and strongly implying destructive or unpleasant weather.
definitions.STYLE: Senses relating to a thin, pointed object.
definitions.SWEET: The basic taste sensation induced by sugar.
definitions.SWIFT: A small plain-colored bird of the family Apodidae that resembles a swallow and is noted for its rapid flight.
definitions.THINK: An act of thinking; consideration (of something).
definitions.TIGER: Panthera tigris, a large predatory mammal of the cat family, indigenous to Asia.
definitions.TOKEN: Something serving as an expression of something else.
definitions.TOWER: A very tall iron-framed structure, usually painted red and white, on which microwave, radio, satellite, or other communication antennas are installed; mast.
definitions.TRACK: A mark left by something that has passed along.
definitions.TRUCK: A small wheel or roller, specifically the wheel of a gun carriage.
definitions.TRUST: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.
definitions.TULIP: A type of flowering plant, genus Tulipa.
definitions.UNION: The act of uniting or joining two or more things into one.
definitions.VITAL: Relating to, or characteristic of life.
definitions.WASTE: Excess of material, useless by-products or damaged, unsaleable products; garbage; rubbish.
definitions.WATER: A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam.
definitions.WEDGE: One of the simple machines; a piece of material, such as metal or wood, thick at one edge and tapered to a thin edge at the other for insertion in a narrow crevice, used for splitting, tightening, securing, or levering.
definitions.WHEEL: A circular device capable of rotating on its axis, facilitating movement or transportation or performing labour in machines.
definitions.WHILE: An uncertain duration of time, a period of time.
definitions.WHITE: The color/colour of snow or milk; the colour of light containing equal amounts of all visible wavelengths.
definitions.WORLD: (with "the") Human collective existence; existence in general.
definitions.XENON: The chemical element (symbol Xe) with an atomic number of 54. It is a colorless, odorless, unreactive noble gas, used notably in camera flash technology.
definitions.YACHT: A slick and light ship for making pleasure trips or racing on water, having sails but often motor-powered. At times used as a residence offshore on a dock.
definitions.YOUTH: The quality or state of being young.
definitions.ZONED: To divide into or assign sections or areas.
definitions.ZONES: Each of the five regions of the earth's surface into which it was divided by climatic differences, namely the torrid zone (between the tropics), two temperate zones (between the tropics and the polar circles), and two frigid zones (within the polar circles).
